title: Press a rocker switch into a panel cutout with its I mark toward the top edge
instruction: Press the rocker switch into the panel's cutout until it sits flush, with its I mark toward the panel's top edge (the orange band), and let go.
context: Team assemblers (O*NET 51-2092.00, well over 500,000 US workers, BLS) on appliance, power-tool and control-panel lines press rocker switches into panel cutouts by hand all shift, usually with the panel lying flat on the bench. The body has spring tabs that grip the plate's edge, so it must go in square to the cutout, with the printed I half toward the panel's top edge, and be pushed home until the flange lies on the plate. A switch fitted half a turn round works the wrong way, and one pushed in crooked or left proud falls out on the first press.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up; arm bases at y +30.5 cm and -30.5 cm. All heights are above the table top. (1) Panel: a grey steel plate 100 (x) x 160 (y) x 1.5 mm lying flat on two steel rails 15 mm wide (x) and 40 mm high that run along y under its near and far edges, so its top is 41.5 mm up and there is open space under it. Its centre is at x 360 mm, y +220 mm. A rectangular cutout 22.0 (x) x 30.0 (y) mm with square corners is at the plate's centre. An orange band 10 mm wide runs along y on the plate's far edge: that edge is the panel's top edge. The panel is bolted down and does not move. (2) Rocker switch: generic KCD1-101 type, 20 A 250 V, black, 12 g. Body 28.0 (y) x 20.5 (x) x 25 mm deep with its rear edges eased 2 mm; flange 31 (y) x 25 (x) x 1.5 mm; rocker 25 (y) x 18 (x), 8 mm proud of the flange, with a white I printed on its half toward the top edge and a white O on the other half (sizes est from catalogues; measure the real part). The body has 0.75 mm of play each side along x and 1.0 mm along y in the cutout. It stands on its rear face on a foam pad (80 x 60 x 10 mm, grey-blue) centred at x 200 mm, y +220 mm, rocker up, turned so the I half points toward the robot (the panel's bottom edge): it must be picked up, turned half a turn about the vertical and pressed into the cutout. (3) The spring tabs are not modelled: the switch goes in under its own weight and the push of the pads, and sits with its flange on the plate. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: End state, read at the last step from the switch's pose and both grippers. In: the flange's rear face within 0.5 mm of the plate's top at its highest corner, and the switch's centre within 2.5 mm (x) and 3 mm (y) of the cutout's centre. Square: the switch's axis within 3 degrees of the vertical. Orientation: the I half's direction within 20 degrees of +x (toward the orange band) is top; within 20 degrees of -x is bottom. Hands off and held: on every step of the last 1 s both grippers' finger zones are 30 mm or more from the switch, and over that 1 s the switch moves under 0.5 mm and turns under 0.3 degrees (it stays seated with no hand on it). Score 0 if at any time the switch's lowest point is more than 10 mm below the table top (it fell off the table), and 0 unless hands off and held. A switch set down on the table and later installed is not penalised; one that ends upside down or crooked is not in the cutout and scores 0 by the rules below. Otherwise: 1.0 in, square, I toward the top edge; 0.5 in and square but I toward the bottom edge (turned half a turn); 0.25 in the cutout but proud by 0.5 to 3 mm, or crooked 3 to 8 degrees, or turned neither way; 0 otherwise. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. Success: 1.0 held for 1 s. In a real trial: in, a 0.5 mm feeler under the flange at four corners; square, a try-square or the feeler; orientation, a look at the printed I against the orange band; hands off and held, a 30 mm spacer against each hand, 30 fps video of the last 1 s, and a 5 N push up on the body's rear end through the gap between the rails with a spring scale: it must not move 0.5 mm.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The real part's spring tabs are not modelled: no snap force (about 15 N) or retention (about 25 N) exists, so the switch goes in under its weight and the pads' push, and holds by lying flange down on the plate. The rocker is rigid and flat. No wires are fitted; real lines crimp the leads first. Friction 0.40 plastic on steel (est).
reset_notes: Press the switch out of the cutout from behind (squeeze both tabs), stand it on the foam pad at x 200, y +220 mm, rocker up, with the I half toward the robot. Replace a switch whose tabs are bent or whose rocker sticks.
